newsitem.title: FRANCE: British lorry drivers allowed to leave Calais.
newsitem.headline: British lorry drivers allowed to leave Calais.

text.p: A British trade union leader said on Wednesday he had secured the release of some 1,000 British truck drivers stranded in the Channel port of Calais by a blockade of striking French truckers.
David Higginbottom, general secretary of the United Road Transport Union, said the French truckers had agreed to allow their British counterparts to return home on humanitarian grounds.
"The British drivers caught up in the blockade at Calais will be released and will be allowed to return (to Britain)," Higginbottom told Reuters Television in Paris.
After several days trapped at Calais, the condition of some drivers was "pretty awful", he said.
"They don't have the basic things like tea or coffee. They're running out of things like gas cylinders to cook with, so they're in a pretty dreadful situation at the moment."
In a letter to French unions, Higginbottom said the British drivers sympathised with the strikers but needed to get home.
"We were able to agree that their problems were in effect ours," he said after meeting French union officals in Paris.
The strikers are demanding higher pay, shorter working hours and a cut in the retirement age from 60 to 55.

They have set up nearly 200 truck blockades on major routes and blocked refineries and fuel depots around France, closing some petrol stations, forcing factory closures and squeezing supplies of goods like fruit and fish.
The strike, the most serious labour unrest in France this year, is also starting to disrupt mail deliveries and grain imports.
Talks between the unions, employers and the government were continuing on Wednesday.
